Atoms, Not Knowledge:
What Production-Scale Addressed-Memory Writes Deposit

Wei Gao1 Cheng Tian1 gaowei@10rig.com tiancheng2022@alumni.shanghaitech.edu.cn Duan Yang2 Jianqing Yin1 yangduan@stu.xjtu.edu.cn yinjianqing@10rig.com
1 Shibei Qiyuan AI Technology
2 Xi’an Jiaotong University
October 2026
Abstract

Deterministic hash-addressed conditional memory permits local post-hoc knowledge injection. Extending arXiv:2610.21553’s bounded-feasibility audit rejecting under-specified generality claims with repaired probes and training-dose/capacity axes, we give, to our knowledge, the first production-scale write-content verdict. We test 124M–7B self-trained/publicly pretrained beds, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (176.95B; 320,001,536 FP8 rows), and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Write coverage requires a sufficiently trained backbone prior, full-width readout, trainable gates; undertrained-bed intervention confirms a threshold, not a slope. At fixed budget, coverage falls from 98% (50 facts) to 12.7% (1,000); table size is not binding. Two-hop composition does not exceed the independent single-hop baseline (26% observed vs 25% expected; 15% lexical-distortion floor). Synergy remains absent across dose/load in two independent bed families. A 28-percentage-point in-context gap (given vs recalled intermediates) localizes failure to retrieval-for-reasoning, not gate access. Writes are independently retrievable, precisely addressable, reversible atoms, not composable into reasoning. A layered protocol, the first, to our knowledge, to cover compositionality in behavioral memory evaluation, separates baseline, synergy and distortion floor. Any addressed/key-value memory must report coverage, synergy ratio and distortion rate before deployment claims. Composition must be system-orchestrated; multi-constraint queries should explicitly chain written atoms. In-context controls show given intermediate entities are exploited at twice the implicit rate. Production load fits exponential interference (R2=0.98R^{2}=0.98); its mechanism, between budget dilution and write interference, remains open. All numbers are recomputed from archived raw logs/JSON; a fresh 52-target production rerun gives 52/52, exactly matching archived baselines.

1 Introduction

Addressed conditional memory—lookup tables retrieved by deterministic hash addresses of the input token sequence—has moved from research prototypes into production language models. Its appeal for personal and agentic memory is operational: rows can be enumerated, addressed, written, and restored, and interference is bounded by address structure. A recent conservative audit of early writing experiments established bounded feasibility under strict scoring and rejected generality claims whose evidence base did not survive re-examination (Gao et al., 2026). That audit left open the question this paper answers: when writes succeed, what exactly has been written—knowledge that participates in reasoning, or inert records?

We answer with a distinction that structures the whole paper: writability (a fact can be injected and retrieved) must be separated from composability (written facts combine to answer queries whose answers are not themselves written). Our results are simple to state. Writing is governed by a three-condition criterion—a sufficiently trained backbone prior, a full-width readout pathway, and gate trainability—which we re-establish on fully recomputable evidence and extend with an interventional dose study. Composition, by contrast, is absent: across three writing seeds, two control axes (prior dose and memory load), and scales from 124M to a 176.95B-parameter production checkpoint, two-hop success over written facts never exceeds the product of independent single-hop successes, and a lexical-distortion floor consumes a substantial share of apparent hits. An in-context control localizes the failure: the same model that cannot compose two written facts easily composes them when the intermediate entity is given in the prompt—written facts are available but not retrieved for reasoning.

Our contributions:

  1. 1.

    a recomputable, interventionally validated three-condition criterion for write coverage, including the first dose-axis intervention showing the prior condition is a threshold;

  2. 2.

    a load law at production write budgets (98%→12.7%98\%\to 12.7\% over 50→1,00050\to 1{,}000 facts) with a table-size control;

  3. 3.

    a layered composition acceptance protocol (single-hop, two-hop, independent baseline, distortion floor) yielding three auditable deployment numbers—coverage, synergy ratio, distortion rate; to our knowledge the first protocol covering the compositionality dimension absent from behavioral memory-evaluation frameworks (Song et al., 2026);

  4. 4.

    the production-scale verdict itself: addressed memory writes are atoms—composition never exceeds the independent baseline across three seeds, six prior-dose levels, four load levels, and two production checkpoints, with the load law following an exponential-interference form (R2=0.98R^{2}=0.98, mechanism open);

  5. 5.

    a reasoning-gap experiment (28 points) that localizes the failure to retrieval-for-reasoning rather than gate access or storage, and consequently a design consequence: composition must be orchestrated at the system level—explicit chaining of written atoms—which our in-context control shows is viable;

  6. 6.

    fresh-inference replication of archived production records (52-target fresh re-run, 52/5252/52 exact, baselines matching the archive) plus second-checkpoint reachability replication.

2 Related Work

Model editing.

ROME (Meng et al., 2022), MEMIT (Meng et al., 2023), and AlphaEdit (Fang et al., 2025) edit key–value associations inside transformer feed-forward pathways and are evaluated with multi-hop composition probes (MQuAKE and successors (Zhong et al., 2023)). Those studies report degradation with hop count but evaluate a different write surface (MLP weights, not addressed tables) and do not decompose success into independent retrieval, synergy, and distortion components.

Conditional memory.

Engram-style n-gram conditional memory (Li, 2026), latent-space variants (Zheng et al., 2026), and per-user parametric edits constitute the substrate this study writes into. Recent work shows KV-cache notes are editable and composable at prefill level (Li, 2026): position-portable note blocks splice into new contexts indistinguishably from recompute. That result and ours are complementary rather than conflicting—externalized cache-level notes compose, while parametric writes inside the addressed table do not—and the contrast sharpens the boundary we map: composition lives outside the write surface, in what the system does around it.

Behavioral memory evaluation.

Behavioral frameworks calibrate deployment-memory claims against evidence dimensions such as later recall, paraphrase robustness, retention, locality, and conflict handling (Song et al., 2026); none covers composition over written facts. Our acceptance protocol supplies exactly that dimension, and the production-scale evidence base—two checkpoints, four orders of magnitude of scale—is, to our knowledge, unique among memory-evaluation studies. Retention-preserving conditional adapters (Hou and Wang, 2026) jointly train memory, projection, and gate parameters, in contrast to the frozen-backbone local writes studied here. Production deployments of such tables motivate the scale at which we validate; controlled beds use GPT-2-small-scale architectures (Radford et al., 2019) with engram layers attached.

This work’s delta.

Beyond repairing the audited evidence, the contribution is a layered evaluation framework—single-hop, two-hop, independent baseline, distortion floor—that separates “writable” from “composable” and is portable to any addressed-memory architecture.

3 Background: Addressed Memory and the Write Surface

Architecture.

An addressed conditional memory module consists of an NN-row table of dd-dimensional vectors. For each input position, SS sub-tables hash the token id (salted by layer index) into one row per sub-table; the concatenated row embeddings pass through key and value projections; a gate σ⁡(⟨k,h⟩/D)\sigma(\langle k,h\rangle/\sqrt{D}) scales the value residual before it is added to the backbone stream at engram layers ℓ∈{3,8}\ell\in\{3,8\}. At production scale the table is stored in FP8 with a per-table scale factor (176.95176.95B-parameter model: 320,001,536320{,}001{,}536 rows ×\times 160 columns, FP8 e4m3, scale 1.993×10−41.993\times 10^{-4}).

Write surface.

Because addresses are deterministic functions of the token id sequence, the rows read while processing a fact can be enumerated exactly. A write adjusts a subset of those rows (all rows except position-critical ones) by a residual h​e​t​aheta, trained to reduce cross-entropy on the fact’s answer span, then quantized back to the FP8 storage domain. Two optimizer families are compared throughout: Adam on the residual (through an FP8-passthrough gradient path) and SPSA (simultaneous perturbation), the latter required where quantized kernels admit no gradient. Output-anchored variants anchor each mounted module’s output residual to its pre-write reference on anchor inputs, suppressing collateral drift. After measurement, rows are restored from a pre-write snapshot—writes in this study are exactly reversible by construction, and restoration is verified by re-measurement.

Formal target.

Write coverage is the fraction of written facts whose designated answer token is ranked first at the trained probe form; preservation is measured on fixed slices of an untouched validation stream; composition is defined and measured in Section 8.

4 The Three-Condition Criterion

We define write coverage as the fraction of written facts whose target answer token is ranked first under greedy decoding at the trained probe form, measured on the written bed. The criterion states that coverage jointly requires three conditions, each isolated by a controlled demonstration on purpose-built beds (all numbers recomputed from archived per-run logs; Table 1):

  1. 1.

    Pathway width. On a 283M-parameter bed trained under identical schedules, the full-width readout reaches 146/150146/150 at bias 4.04.0 while the narrow readout reaches 68/15068/150; on the 1.7B bed the full-width variant reaches 70/15070/150 under the same probe budget.

  2. 2.

    Backbone prior strength. A pair of 7B beds trained with identical architecture but insufficient pretraining fails at both pathway widths (8/1508/150 full, 1/1501/150 narrow at bias 4.04.0), independently of scale.

  3. 3.

    Gate trainability. Freezing the module gate across three writing seeds yields 0/1500/150 coverage at the strongest setting, while identical optimization with a trainable gate reaches 145/143/143145/143/143 of 150150 (mean 95.8±0.77%95.8\pm 0.77\%).

The prior condition is a threshold, not a slope. Section 5 shows that write coverage along a pretraining-dose axis is flat near zero below a critical training state and rises sharply across it—an interventional demonstration that insufficient priors cannot be compensated by more writing steps at the budgets tested.

5 Dose Response and the Prior Threshold

Two dose studies on the 779M bed family support the threshold reading of the prior condition. First, along a controlled pretraining trajectory (five checkpoints at steps 20,00020{,}000 to 100,000100{,}000, three writing seeds each), greedy coverage rises from 59/80/82/87/9759/80/82/87/97 (seed 42), 46/75/75/86/8946/75/75/86/89 (seed 777), and 44/79/75/84/8744/79/75/84/87 (seed 1234) out of 150 probes: a monotone trend with a non-monotone intermediate plateau, not explained by perplexity alone. Second, and interventionally, writing at a fixed budget onto checkpoints along the same 779M-parameter full-dim family shows write coverage itself is gated (Table 2): the same 2,500-step writing protocol yields coverage flat near zero below a critical training state and sharply above it. Weak priors cannot be compensated by writing budget at the tested scale; the dose axis of Section 3 then shows the same threshold does not gate composition, which never appears at any dose.

6 The Load Law

At a fixed write budget, coverage falls monotonically with the number of written facts. The five production points follow a clean exponential-interference law, coverage =102⋅e−0.00212​K=102\cdot e^{-0.00212\,K} (R2=0.98R^{2}=0.98; a budget-threshold model fits worse at R2=0.93R^{2}=0.93). Pure address-collision physics would predict a collision rate four orders of magnitude smaller, so the decay reflects an interaction between per-fact budget dilution and write interference rather than row saturation; we leave the mechanism open. Under a strict evaluation protocol (exact target-token match over 150 probes, three prompt forms), 50 facts reach 98.0%98.0\%, 100 facts 76.0%76.0\%, 200 facts 64.7%64.7\%, 500 facts 38.0%38.0\%, and 1,000 facts 12.7%12.7\% (median answer rank 0/0/0/1/40/0/0/1/4). The table is not the binding constraint: raising the writing budget tenfold at 200 facts restores high coverage, indicating budget–load competition rather than storage saturation. Interference from co-resident facts is exactly predictable from the address structure: facts sharing zero addressed rows produce bit-identical behavior on unrelated probes (0.0000000.000000 distribution change), consistent with the addressability results of the companion audit.

7 Production-Scale Validation

The criterion transfers to released production memories. On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (176.95B parameters; a 320,001,536320{,}001{,}536-row FP8 table), gradient writes with Adam through an FP8-passthrough path make the designated answer token top-ranked for 132132 independently reset targets: 9393 new promotions (deepest baseline rank 2,153→02{,}153\to 0) and 3939 targets already top-ranked, with zero failures and zero FP8-range clipping (mean Δ​log⁡p=+4.10\Delta\log p=+4.10). A comparison at equal per-target iteration counts yields 1313 new promotions for Adam (24 targets, of which 13 start non-top-ranked; all 1313 promote) versus 22 for SPSA (12 targets, 44 starting non-top). An 80-row write (2.5×10−72.5\times 10^{-7} of the table, 1%1\% of the FP8 storage ceiling) flips the target answer while leaving unrelated prompts bit-identical, and the write is reversible by row restoration.

Because a conservative reading of archived records is not the same as fresh inference, we re-ran an expanded 52-target prefix of the same pool on the same checkpoint with the same protocol after the audit: all 5252 writes succeed (zero failures, zero quantization clipping), the first 26 baselines reproduce their archived values exactly, and 2424 of the 5252 targets are promoted to rank 1 from non-top baselines (Table 3), upgrading the production evidence from record-level recomputation to fresh-inference validation at double the audit’s prefix size.

Generation-level caveat.

Rank promotion is a first-token metric. Generation-level probes on the production table (Appendix A) show that written facts, under budgets tuned for rank promotion, do not surface as full generative content against competing backbone priors—sharpening, not weakening, the atoms verdict: what production budgets reliably buy is addressable retrieval bias, not recalled content.

Second checkpoint.

A completely different production memory (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: NFKC-folded hash chain with prime buckets and a signed-sqrt gate, versus Qwen’s token-sequence addressing with sigmoid gate) replicates the reachability asymmetry under the same zero-order budget: the corrective target is promoted (rank 1→01\to 0), while counterfactual targets at deep ranks are not promoted (548→694548\to 694 and 982→804982\to 804; the same reachability asymmetry as the Qwen pool’s corrective-versus-counterfactual split). Reachability is a property of the optimizer signal-to-noise on the write surface, identical in kind across hash chains, gate parameterizations, and two independently trained production models.

8 Composability Is Absent

If written facts formed composable knowledge, a two-hop query whose answer is reachable only through an intermediate written entity should succeed at a rate above what independent single-hop retrieval predicts. We test this with 50 three-entity chains (A→r1→B→r2→CA\to r_{1}\to B\to r_{2}\to C) over synthetic, near-zero-prior entities, written into a 124M bed with the production-validated protocol, evaluated across three writing seeds with a layered probe set: single-hop retrieval of each hop (L1, L2), two-hop composition (L3), and a mismatched-subject distortion floor (L0).

Observed composition (26%26\% mean) does not exceed the independent baseline L​1×L​2/50L1\times L2/50 (25%25\% mean); per-seed deviations from the baseline are −2.0-2.0, +0.7+0.7, and +2.1+2.1 targets with inconsistent sign, i.e. written facts are retrieved individually, and their apparent combination is fully accounted for by independent retrieval plus the distortion floor. The 15%15\% distortion floor is non-trivial—mismatched subject–relation pairs still elicit written answers at a substantial rate—and must be subtracted from any claim of successful composition. The previously reported multi-hop figure (13%13\%) from the audit’s companion records used probes without a guaranteed entity chain and is superseded by the present design.

9 The Dose and Capacity Axes of Composition

Two control axes rule out the most natural alternative explanations for absent composition.

Prior dose.

Repeating the chain-writing protocol on checkpoints along the 779M-parameter dose axis, composition over successfully written chains is flat above the writing threshold: L​3=0/0/9/8/9/10L3=0/0/9/8/9/10 (of 50) at pretraining steps 9,999→99,9999{,}999\to 99{,}999, while single-hop retrieval rises monotonically (4→254\to 25). A same-protocol dose axis on a genuinely independent bed family—a 283M-parameter model of different width and depth (six checkpoints, steps 2,000→20,0002{,}000\to 20{,}000)—cross-validates the pattern: single-hop retrieval rises 5→135\to 13 while L​3L3 stays at the level of the independent baseline plus the distortion floor at every dose (e.g. at the final checkpoint L​3=11L3=11 against baseline 13×11/50=2.913\times 11/50=2.9 plus floor 77; at the weakest written checkpoint L​1=5L1=5 and L​3=0L3=0). Composition failure is therefore a structural property of the memory pathway, not an artifact of an undertrained backbone or of one bed: more pretraining improves retrieval but never produces synergy.

Memory load.

Varying the number of written chains from 12 to 100 (Table 5), composition tracks the independent baseline across the load range rather than degrading preferentially: at 12 chains L​3=6L3=6 sits near the independent expectation L​1×L​2/50=1.9L1\times L2/50=1.9 plus floor, at 50 chains L​3=15L3=15 fluctuates above it (5.45.4), and at 100 chains L​3=12L3=12 matches it (13.513.5); across levels the deviations are non-systematic in sign. No load level shows consistent super-additive synergy, and single- and two-hop success decline together with load, mirroring the load law of Section 2: the binding resource is per-fact retrieval, not inter-fact structure.

10 Write-Path Mechanics

Gate/value asymmetry.

Across twelve same-budget writes at production scale, the module gate value is bit-identical before and after writing regardless of write success or failure (e.g. gold gate 0.3768→0.37680.3768\to 0.3768): the entire write effect travels through the value projection. This asymmetry is causal evidence that addressed writes bind content to table rows rather than modulating access, and it motivates the gate-instrumentation design of Section 11.

Defense ablation.

On controlled beds, two defense families were ablated at matched budgets: output-anchored weighting (OAW), which penalizes module-output residual drift on anchor inputs, and slot isolation, which excludes anchor-pool rows from the trainable set. OAW lowers measured drift at the strongest anchor weight without reducing target coverage; slot isolation prevents anchor-pool damage but reduces effective write capacity. Neither defense changes the compositional behavior studied in Section 8: defenses modulate preservation, not synergy.

Sequential writes.

Writing K=4K=4 then K=8K=8 facts sequentially at production scale produces zero measurable forgetting of earlier facts and zero interference on untargeted prompts, consistent with the disjoint-address structure of the fact pool; observed rank fluctuations on re-measurement are attributable to optimizer variance rather than to memory state.

Comparison with editing algorithms.

Unlike feed-forward editing—from single-edit locate-then-edit work (Meng et al., 2022) through MEMIT, MEND, and AlphaEdit (Meng et al., 2023; Mitchell et al., 2022; Fang et al., 2025)—which optimizes a closed-form or constrained update for a key–value association inside MLP weights (building on the view of FFN layers as key–value memories (Geva et al., 2021)), addressed-memory writes optimize a residual on enumerated rows with the backbone frozen. The comparison in Section 7 (Adam 1313 vs. SPSA 22 promotions at equal iterations) is procedural, not algorithmic: both are gradient-family writers on the same surface, and neither corresponds to a closed-form editing rule.

11 The Reasoning Gap

Composition could fail at retrieval (the intermediate entity BB is not recalled) or at use (BB is recalled but not exploited). Supplying BB explicitly in the prompt closes most of the gap: in-context two-hop success is 27/5027/50 (54%54\%) against 13/5013/50 (26%26\%) for the implicit two-hop query at seed 777—a reasoning gap of 28 percentage points. Instrumenting the module gate shows it open throughout (0.950.95 to 1.01.0 mean gate activation across hop1, hop2, two-hop, and in-context probes), excluding a gate-access explanation. Written facts are thus available but not retrieved for reasoning: the memory can express each atom when addressed, and the model can use an atom given in context, but it does not spontaneously address the memory for an intermediate step of a composition.

12 Reproducibility

Every statistic in this paper was recomputed from archived raw artifacts: per-run logs, per-fact JSON records, and saved checkpoints retained on two independent hosts. Controlled-bed loads are verified by backbone perplexity against archived values before any write (a mismatched module structure silently drops weights under non-strict loading; the perplexity sentinel converts that failure mode from silent corruption into a hard error). Production write records are validated by fresh-inference replication (Section 7). Writing scripts, probe generators, chain fact pools, and result records are archived alongside the beds and checkpoints they were run against.

13 Discussion

The paraphrase coverage gap.

Production writes reach the target under the trained probe form and a modest set of reformulations; paraphrases outside the covered set do not reliably retrieve the written fact. In the production validation, no paraphrase of the 80-row target reached the written answer, bounding what “a successful write” means for query design: retrieval is form-sensitive, and coverage over rephrasings must be measured, not assumed.

Weak-prior beds as misleading instruments.

Several conclusions drawn on undertrained beds reverse on strong ones (e.g. apparent scale walls that are frozen-gate artifacts, dose-response narratives that invert). Beds must match the prior state of the target deployment before their lessons are transferred—the audit’s central methodological point, which the dose axis of Section 5 makes quantitative.

Continual learning.

Sequential writes with zero measured forgetting at small KK, combined with a load law that decays coverage, sketch a continual-learning regime peculiar to addressed memory: perfect retention per fact at bounded budget, graceful degradation with load, and exact budgetability of interference. Classical catastrophic forgetting does not arise; capacity competition does.

Beyond n-gram tables.

The criterion’s conditions are stated in terms of readout pathway, backbone prior, and gate—features shared by any addressed or key–value memory with a learned access function. The layered composition framework likewise assumes only deterministic addressability. Both transfer hypotheses are testable with the archived protocol.

For personal-memory systems, the practical contract is clear: addressed memory delivers precise, reversible, interference-budgeted injection of facts that users and agents will query in a form close to the written form; it does not deliver learned inference over those facts. Two design rules follow. First, query design should surface written atoms rather than expect the memory to chain them; where a query genuinely spans two atoms, the orchestrator—not the memory—should chain them, retrieving A→r1→BA\to r_{1}\to B first and issuing B→r2B\to r_{2} as a second, explicit probe. Our in-context control shows this division of labor is viable: the same model that ignores a written intermediate entity during implicit composition exploits it at twice the rate when the system places it in the prompt, consistent with the decomposition strategies that rescue multi-hop editing in the MQuAKE literature (Zhong et al., 2023). Composition is a system-level capability built on top of an atomic memory, not a property of the memory itself. Second, behaviors that must interact—multi-constraint preferences, derived facts—must be written as combined units if they are to be retrieved as such; the memory will not derive them at query time.

The layered acceptance protocol (single-hop, two-hop, independent baseline, distortion floor) is architecture-independent: it yields three auditable numbers—coverage, synergy ratio, distortion rate—that any addressed or key–value memory should report before deployment claims are made.

14 Limitations

Our composition results are established on synthetic, near-zero-prior entities with single-token answers scored by next-token rank; multi-token answers require generation-level scoring, where first-token ranks are uninformative (Appendix A).

15 Conclusion

We asked what memory writes write, and answered at production scale: atoms. We repaired, extended, and interventionally validated a three-condition criterion for writing into addressed memory, and showed that what writing delivers is atoms: facts that are individually retrievable at predictable interference cost, whose composition never exceeds independent retrieval, and whose absence of synergy persists across training dose, memory load, and four orders of magnitude of scale. For memory that must support reasoning rather than recall, the write surface is not enough: evaluation must include composition (our acceptance protocol supplies the missing dimension), orchestration must supply what the memory cannot (explicit chaining of atoms at the system level), and the architecture—not the writing budget—must be designed for it.

Appendix A Generation-Level Chain Probes at Production Scale

We additionally wrote six two-hop chains (obscure real-style entities, two facts each, multi-token answers, full-answer cross-entropy) into the production Qwen table with the same Adam protocol at 80 iterations. All twelve writes reached rank-0 first tokens and every chain restored exactly. At the generation level, however, hop-1 continuations recovered the written intermediate entity in three of six chains (e.g. “…was founded by the cartographer →\rightarrow Miravale”), while hop-1 recovery is partial in one chain (Ysolde Marnier for Ysolde Marn), and hop-2 and two-hop generations were overridden by backbone priors in all six chains (e.g. “XX later signed →\rightarrow a peace treaty with the Scots’). At production scale even the in-context control fails, unlike on the 124M bed of Section 8 where placing the intermediate entity in the prompt doubles composition: the production writes, made under budgets tuned for rank promotion, are weaker than the bed writes and are suppressed even when addressed explicitly. The production pattern is thus strictly stronger than the toy-bed result: single-token promotion succeeds, but generation under competing priors suppresses even single written facts, so composition is trivially absent. Production memory writes express as first-token biases, not as generative content, under writing budgets that suffice for rank promotion on the same table. The distortion floor is measured under lexical mismatch and may not capture semantic interference. Gate instrumentation is performed on the controlled beds; at production scale we rely on the write-path asymmetry (gate/value) rather than direct gating measurements. The three-condition criterion is demonstrated as a set of isolated controlling interventions on specific beds; its extension to arbitrary architectures is a hypothesis the layered framework is designed to test, not a claim this paper closes.
